newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says new govt bond issues may be hard to avoid.
newsitem.headline: MOF says new govt bond issues may be hard to avoid.

text.p: Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Monday that it may be difficult for the government to avoid issuing bonds to finance the state budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year from next April 1.
Asked whether Japan would need to issue deficit-financing bonds to finance the budget, Ogawa said that looking at state finances, it would be "extremely difficult" to avoid doing so.
"However, we would like to make our best efforts to avoid large issues of government bonds, including deficit-financing bonds," he said.
Ogawa reiterated his view that he did not think it was yet necessary to start considering any supplementary budget for this fiscal year, as economic prospects were brighter.
Another MOF official told reporters that the ministry had not started any procedures to create a supplementary budget.
